summary:
The Autism Collaboration, Accountability, Research, Education, and Support Act of 2024 (Public Law 118-180) amends the Public Health Service Act (PHSA) to expand, modify, and reauthorize federal activities and programs relating to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) through fiscal year 2029.

Section 2 amends Section 409C of the PHSA (42 U.S.C. 284g) regarding National Institutes of Health (NIH) activities. It expands the scope of research under subsection (a)(1) to require consultation with relevant federal agencies and to include fields such as psychiatry, psychology, developmental behavioral pediatrics, audiology, and gerontology. It mandates that research investigate services and supports across the lifespan, examine supports for caregivers, and reflect the entire ASD population, including those with co-occurring conditions. Subsection (b) increases the number of Centers of Excellence from five to seven and adds gerontology to their required fields. Subsection (d) is amended to require the NIH Director to provide mechanisms for public input and issue guidance on public engagement. A new subsection (e) requires the Director to submit annual budget estimates for FY2026 through FY2029 directly to the President for transmittal to Congress.

Section 3 amends several PHSA provisions. Section 399AA (42 U.S.C. 280i) is amended to extend the Developmental Disabilities Surveillance and Research Program authorization to September 30, 2029, and to specify research applies across the lifespan. Section 399BB (42 U.S.C. 280i-1) updates terminology (e.g., "culturally and linguistically appropriate information," "increased likelihood") and amends intervention grant authorities to develop and evaluate evidence-based practices across the lifespan. It requires the Secretary to submit a report to Congress within two years of enactment on the feasibility of expanding developmental-behavioral pediatrician training programs. Section 399CC (42 U.S.C. 280i-2) modifies the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee's duties to require a strategic plan with proposed budgetary requirements and annual or biennial updates to Congress. Section 399DD (42 U.S.C. 280i-3) requires a progress report within four years of September 30, 2024, renames the "Health and Well-Being" report to the "Mental Health Needs" report, and requires a report within two years of enactment on young adults transitioning to adulthood. 

Section 3(e) amends Section 399EE (42 U.S.C. 280i-4) to authorize appropriations for FY2025 through FY2029: $28,100,000 for surveillance, $56,344,000 for education and early detection, and $306,000,000 for NIH activities. 

Section 4 authorizes the HHS Secretary to provide training and technical assistance to states, Indian Tribes, localities, or territories on utilizing federal funding for evidence-based communication tools for individuals with ASD, and requires an annual report to Congress summarizing such assistance.
